title: Ebola crosses borders: from DR Congo to Nigeria and Kenya
deck: A Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak that has passed 10,000 confirmed cases in DR Congo has sent patients to Nigeria and Kenya, and the WHO calls the response 'complex'. Africa is keeping borders open and betting on surveillance, while some states and airlines tighten rules.

fuel.title: DR Congo Ebola cases pass 10,000
fuel.how: A source outbreak this large, with about 4,900 deaths reported, keeps producing travellers who can carry the virus out of the region.

fuel.title: Health ministers keep borders open
fuel.how: African ministers chose surveillance over travel bans, so people keep moving and detection at airports and roads carries the load.

fuel.title: CAR tightens border checks with DR Congo
fuel.how: Stricter checks slow cross-border movement and trade, and show governments are not all following the open-borders line.

fuel.title: Nurse killed; responders under pressure
fuel.how: Attacks on and strain among health workers weaken the contact tracing and care that stop the virus spreading.

card.headline: Ebola has jumped from DR Congo to Nigeria and Kenya, and airports are now the front line

keyNumber.label: confirmed Ebola cases in DR Congo, with about 4,900 deaths reported (28 October)

forYou.line: Expect health screening at airports and bus stations. Rules differ by country and change quickly, so check before you fly.
Contact tracing and 21-day monitoring are the main tools. Kenya has already released 20 contacts after a full monitoring period.
Plan for patchy border rules. Some countries are tightening checks even though African health ministers back open borders.
The outbreak is huge in DR Congo, but the new cases in Kenya look steadier. Kenya reports 10 days without new cases.

effects.text: Confirmed cases pass 10,000 in DR Congo; the WHO urges sustained effort and a UN official reportedly says growth is 'exponential'
Nigerian and Kenyan patients may have crossed paths at Uganda's airport, putting transit hubs in the spotlight
African health ministers agree to keep borders open and rely on surveillance
The Central African Republic tightens checks on its border with DR Congo
A nurse is killed in DR Congo; responders are described as under pressure
Nigerian states such as Kano and Anambra deploy surveillance officers at motor parks and train staff
Further travel restrictions reported across Africa and worldwide, a patchwork of rules for airlines and travellers
Kenya runs a 21-day contact quarantine and awaits a 42-day countdown; a vaccine trial starts in Congo, but protection is delayed
Sport schedules wobble: Nigeria's U23 first leg in DR Congo is in doubt
Africa CDC warns the disease could reach the UK and spread like Covid unless preparedness is funded
Pressure for emergency funding and vaccine access grows; Russia and DR Congo discuss fast-tracking a vaccine
Distrust of authorities may undermine the response; one commentary says Ebola is outrunning Congo's trust faster than its health system

whatHappened: An Ebola outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo virus has grown in DR Congo, and on 28 October it passed 10,000 confirmed cases and about 4,900 deaths, according to reports quoting the WHO. To our knowledge, earlier Bundibugyo outbreaks were far smaller.

On 23 October the WHO said Africa faces a 'complex' outbreak after the virus reached Nigeria. Kenya had also recorded a case. Officials told the BBC that the Nigerian and Kenyan patients may have crossed paths at Uganda's airport.

Since then Kenya has had a calmer week. It reports 10 days with no new cases, released 20 contacts of its first patient after 21 days of monitoring, and is waiting for a 42-day countdown. Nigerian states are screening at motor parks. A vaccine trial has begun in Congo, but vaccines are not yet widely available.
whyItMatters: People on the move: the source outbreak is large and growing, and a UN official is reported to call it exponential. Every infected traveller can carry the virus through a hub such as Uganda's airport. The possible link between the Nigerian and Kenyan patients shows how quickly one hub can touch two countries.

Politics: African health ministers agreed to keep borders open and rely on surveillance instead of bans. That protects trade and movement, but it puts weight on screening, contact tracing and public trust. A Congo commentary warns that trust is falling faster than the health system can cope.

Trade and shipping: not everyone is following the same line. The Central African Republic has tightened border checks with DR Congo, and travel industry reports describe more restrictions across Africa and worldwide. A patchwork of rules is hard for airlines, truckers and travellers to plan around.

Security: a nurse was killed in DR Congo and the UN says responders are under pressure. Attacks, fear and fatigue reduce contact tracing and care, which are the things that actually stop an outbreak. The Africa CDC head warns of wider spread unless funding rises.

winners.why: Screening at airports, bus stations and motor parks creates demand for testing, protective gear and training.
A trial has started in Congo and Russia and DR Congo are discussing fast-tracking registration of a vaccine.
Africa CDC commended Kenya's containment, and the country reports 10 days without new cases.

losers.why: They carry most of the burden: over 10,000 confirmed cases, about 4,900 deaths and strained responders.
A nurse was killed and a doctor died of Ebola, according to Africa CDC reports.

losers.who: Airlines, travel firms and cross-border traders
losers.why: New restrictions and extra checks add cost and uncertainty, and the rules differ by country.
Nigeria's U23 match in DR Congo is in doubt over the Ebola scare.

whatsNext: 11 November: Kenya targets the release of its remaining Ebola contacts, if no new cases appear.
Kenya awaits a 42-day countdown, the usual way to declare a chain of transmission over. Timing depends on the date of the last case.
Weeks ahead: the new vaccine trial in Congo, and talks on fast-tracking vaccine registration.
Ongoing: case counts in DR Congo, any new case in Nigeria, Uganda or a fifth country, and whether more states copy the Central African Republic's border checks.

predict.question: Before you read the scenarios: what is the most likely path over the next three months?
options: Spillovers stay contained to a few imported cases
A major city outbreak outside DR Congo
A case turns up outside Africa
predict.explanation: Our base case, at about 45%, is that Nigeria and Kenya stay contained while DR Congo's outbreak keeps growing. Kenya's quiet run and Nigeria's screening support it. Further African spread is next at about 35%. All probabilities are author judgement.

timeline.title: MSF's Ituri treatment centre starts treating confirmed cases
timeline.detail: Approximate. MSF later said its centre had no confirmed cases under treatment for the first time since May, which suggests the outbreak was already running by then.

timeline.title: Guardian explainer on an Ebola outbreak in DR Congo and Uganda
timeline.detail: The article's link says the WHO described an outbreak in both countries. We rely only on that headline-level detail.

timeline.title: Responders under pressure as outbreak expands
timeline.detail: UN News reports strain on Ebola responders in DR Congo as the outbreak widens.

timeline.title: WHO calls outbreak 'complex' after spread to Nigeria
timeline.detail: Kenya has also reported a case. Officials say the Nigerian and Kenyan patients may have crossed paths at Uganda's airport.

timeline.title: Nurse killed in DR Congo
timeline.detail: The UN Ebola coordinator and WHO head condemn the killing of a nurse working to stop the disease.

timeline.title: 20 Kenyan contacts released from quarantine
timeline.detail: They finished a mandatory 21-day monitoring period after Kenya's first Bundibugyo case.

timeline.title: DR Congo passes 10,000 confirmed cases
timeline.detail: The WHO urges sustained efforts. The same day Africa CDC's Jean Kaseya warns the outbreak could reach the UK without more funding.

timeline.title: Ministers keep borders open; CAR tightens checks
timeline.detail: African health ministers favour surveillance over travel restrictions. The Central African Republic tightens border checks with DR Congo. A DW headline quotes the UN saying the outbreak is 'growing exponentially'.

timeline.title: Vaccine trial begins in Congo; Kenya reports a quiet spell
timeline.detail: Reports say vaccines are not yet widely available. Kenya has gone 10 days without new cases and targets 11 November to release contacts. Kano is deploying surveillance officers at motor parks.

causes.name: Fragile health systems
causes.detail: Eastern DR Congo has long had limited health capacity; responders are described as stretched.

causes.name: Insecurity and distrust
causes.detail: A nurse was killed, and commentary says Ebola is outrunning Congo's trust faster than its health system.

causes.name: Busy air and road links
causes.detail: Hubs like Uganda's airport and motor parks in Nigeria move many people between countries each day.

causes.name: Bundibugyo outbreak in DR Congo
causes.detail: Over 10,000 confirmed cases and about 4,900 deaths. To our knowledge this is far larger than any earlier Bundibugyo outbreak.

causes.name: No widely available vaccine
causes.detail: A trial has begun, but protection is delayed; this is our understanding of the Bundibugyo strain, not a number in the sources.

causes.name: Travel through a shared hub
causes.detail: Patients now in Nigeria and Kenya may have crossed paths at Uganda's airport.

causes.name: Funding gap
causes.detail: Africa CDC says the disease could spread like Covid unless funding for preparedness and treatment is secured.

causes.name: Mixed border policy
causes.detail: Ministers say keep borders open, while the Central African Republic tightens checks and travel firms report new restrictions.

stakeholders.name: World Health Organization
stakeholders.wants: Contain spread and sustain the response
stakeholders.likelyMove: Keep calling for sustained effort and argue against blanket travel bans

stakeholders.name: Africa CDC (Jean Kaseya)
stakeholders.leverage: Public warnings, support to states such as Kenya
stakeholders.likelyMove: Press donors, back surveillance over bans

stakeholders.name: DR Congo government and responders (including MSF)
stakeholders.wants: Break chains of transmission and win trust
stakeholders.leverage: Control of the response; vaccine registration talks with Russia
stakeholders.likelyMove: Expand treatment, vaccine trials and community outreach

stakeholders.name: Nigerian federal and state authorities
stakeholders.leverage: Surveillance at motor parks; worker training in Kano and Anambra

stakeholders.name: Kenya's Ministry of Health
stakeholders.likelyMove: Release contacts on schedule if no new cases arise, as targeted on 11 November

stakeholders.name: Uganda's airport and health authorities
stakeholders.wants: Avoid being seen as a spread point
stakeholders.likelyMove: Review screening and share traveller data

stakeholders.name: Neighbours such as the Central African Republic
stakeholders.likelyMove: Tighten checks, possibly beyond what the ministers agreed

sectors.why: Hubs like Uganda's airport are under pressure and more screening and restrictions are reported.
Demand surges; responders are stretched and attacked, but quiet spells such as Kenya's and MSF's Ituri discharges show progress.
Tighter checks, such as the Central African Republic's, slow goods and passengers.
A trial has started and Russia and DR Congo discuss fast-tracking registration.
Industry reports note more restrictions across Africa and worldwide.
Nigeria's U23 first leg in DR Congo is in doubt.
Africa CDC says funding is needed to prepare and treat, and the WHO urges sustained effort.

dailyLife.effect: Expect health screening and possible questions about recent travel; transit through hubs like Uganda is under watch.

dailyLife.item: Bus and motor park travel in Nigeria
dailyLife.effect: Kano is deploying surveillance officers at motor parks, so expect temperature checks and questions.

dailyLife.item: Being a contact of a case
dailyLife.effect: In Kenya, contacts face 21 days of mandatory monitoring, then release; the next release target is 11 November.
Nigeria's U23 match against DR Congo is in doubt.
Checks are tighter, so expect delays.

scenarios.name: Contained spillovers
scenarios.looksLike: Nigeria and Kenya record few or no further cases. Kenya completes its 42-day countdown. DR Congo's outbreak stays large but responders gain ground.
signposts: More discharges like MSF's in Ituri
scenarios.effectOnWorld: Travel rules ease slowly. Attention returns to funding and vaccines for DR Congo.

scenarios.name: Further African spread
scenarios.looksLike: One or more additional countries report imported cases, probably through air hubs or border crossings. More states copy the Central African Republic's checks.
signposts: A new country reports a case
Border closures despite the ministers' agreement
scenarios.effectOnWorld: The patchwork of rules becomes costly for trade and travel. Donors face louder funding calls.

scenarios.name: City outbreak outside DR Congo
scenarios.looksLike: Local transmission takes hold in a large city such as Lagos, Kano or Nairobi, overwhelming contact tracing.
signposts: Health worker infections outside DR Congo
scenarios.effectOnWorld: Strong pressure for travel curbs and emergency funding. Economic hits to hosts are larger.

scenarios.name: Case outside Africa
scenarios.looksLike: An imported or medevac case appears in Europe or elsewhere, as Africa CDC has warned about the UK.
signposts: Travel-linked cases in a major hub
scenarios.effectOnWorld: Political attention and funding jump. Screening at airports in rich countries expands.

predictions.text: Kenya will complete its 42-day Ebola countdown with no new cases and declare its outbreak over. Estimated, because the start date of the countdown is not given. Probability 0.5.
DR Congo will report at least 12,000 confirmed Ebola cases. Rough estimate from the pace so far. Probability 0.7.
A country other than DR Congo, Uganda, Nigeria and Kenya will report a confirmed case. Probability 0.35.
African states will not adopt a continental travel ban; the open-borders line from health ministers will hold, though some states keep tighter checks. Probability 0.75.
A confirmed Ebola case will be reported in Europe or the UK. Probability 0.07.

actions: Track country-by-country entry rules and screening before sending staff or freight to or through DR Congo, Uganda, Nigeria or Kenya.
Add buffer time to cross-border routes where checks have tightened, such as the Congo-Central African Republic border.
Prepare a medical and evacuation plan for staff in affected regions.
Watch the number of new countries reporting cases and any airline suspensions, which move travel and trade exposure.
Treat funding announcements and vaccine registration news as signals of how fast the response can scale.
Avoid assuming a quick end: DR Congo's outbreak is still large even if Kenya is quiet.
Before travelling, check official health advisories from your own government and the destination.
Report fever after travel to a health service and mention where you have been.
Follow official updates rather than social media rumours about cases.
Back surveillance, contact tracing and worker safety, as the ministers agreed, rather than blanket bans.
Fund preparedness now; Africa CDC warns that without money the disease could spread widely.
Share traveller data and screening practice between hub airports such as Uganda's, Nairobi and Lagos.
Protect health workers and invest in community trust.

analogues.whatFollowed: About 28,000 cases and 11,000 deaths across Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone, with a few exported cases. Delayed response and mistrust drove its size. Figures are from general knowledge.

analogues.event: Nigeria's Ebola outbreak, imported by air traveller
analogues.whatFollowed: Nigeria contained a case that came through Lagos airport to a small number of cases through rapid contact tracing. Shows imported cases can be stopped in a large city. From general knowledge.

analogues.event: Kivu and Ituri Ebola outbreak in DR Congo
analogues.whatFollowed: About 3,500 cases and over 2,000 deaths amid armed conflict, attacks on responders and community distrust, but a licensed vaccine was deployed. Here the strain is different and vaccines are still in trial. From general knowledge.

watch.title: Kenya contact release target
watch.why: A clean release supports the view that Kenya's spillover is contained.

watch.title: Kenya's 42-day countdown
watch.why: Completion would let Kenya declare its outbreak over; the start date is not in the sources.

watch.title: New cases in Nigeria
watch.why: Kano and Anambra preparations suggest concern; any local transmission would change the outlook.

watch.title: DR Congo case count
watch.why: Passing 10,000 with reports of exponential growth sets the pressure on everything else.

watch.title: Vaccine trial and registration news
watch.why: The trial has started and Russia is in talks over registration; results decide how fast protection arrives.

watch.title: Border and flight rules
watch.why: The Central African Republic has tightened checks; more states following would erode the open-borders line.

watch.title: Responder safety
watch.why: A nurse was killed and a doctor died; further attacks or infections would hit the response.

confidence.claim: DR Congo has passed 10,000 confirmed cases and about 4,900 deaths
confidence.note: Reported by UN News and several outlets, but the deaths figure may mix confirmed and probable cases; the sources do not define it.

confidence.claim: Nigerian and Kenyan patients may have crossed paths at Uganda's airport
confidence.note: The BBC attributes this to officials as a possibility, not a confirmed link.
Based on headlines reporting 10 days without new cases and contact releases; the 42-day countdown has not finished.

confidence.claim: African ministers keep borders open while some states tighten checks
confidence.note: Drawn from headlines and short summaries; individual country rules are not fully documented here.

confidence.claim: Context on past outbreaks and vaccine availability
confidence.note: From general knowledge and rounded; not drawn from the listed sources.
Author judgement, not sourced forecasts; to be graded as events resolve.
The sources say the outbreak spread to Nigeria but the material here gives no case count or current status there.

evidence.method: Drafted from the listed sources and wire headlines up to 30 October 2026. Several items rest on headlines or short summaries, not full article text, so detail on Nigeria, Kenya and border rules is thin. Dates for the start of Kenya's 42-day countdown and for the Nigeria U23 match were not available. Scenario probabilities, prediction odds and the timing of Kenya's possible all-clear are the author's estimates. Background on earlier outbreaks is general knowledge and rounded.
